title: Saʿd ibn Faraj, ruler of the Ṭāʾifa of Qūnka since 1395 and the Emperor's brother-in-law, dies at forty-nine. His daughter Maryam, seventeen, wife of the Emperor's son Saʿd, becomes Shaykha of Qūnka

data.successor: Maryam bint Saʿd, born 5 November 1390 (51/83/69), daughter of Saʿd ibn Faraj and Umm al-Fatḥ

title: The Emperor Ismāʿīl resolves to raise Qurṭuba from its ruins as the Capital of the Old Caliphate, but keeps his court at Ishbīliya. Qurṭuba is given the dignity and the means to rebuild, and Ishbīliya grows richer still

data.text: its streets are filled with crime, its inhabitants curse the decay that has befallen the place, and many old sites remain in ruins after our conflicts with Christian rulers (the game's text)
data.choice: We should keep our Court where it is (the option on Trent's screen; the save of 5 August 1408 confirms the capital still at Ishbīliya)

effects.Qurṭuba: Capital of the Old Caliphate, as long as the realm lasts: raw materials output +15%, local monthly prosperity +1%, local monthly development growth +10%

realm.markets: Ishbīliya ranked first among the markets of the world

source: Trent's screenshot of 1 March 1408; save of 5 August 1408

title: Ismāʿīl ibn Yūsuf, the late Emperor's brother, dies at fifty-four. He had sat in the dīwān from 1382 until 1405

data.diwan: from 1 December 1382 to August 1405, when Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf took his seat

title: The sons of Muḥammad. The heir's two eldest boys, Ismāʿīl and Aḥmad, both five and both gifted, are enough to set aside the thought of changing the succession: if the Emperor Ismāʿīl reigns long, the crown can pass to Muḥammad and on to them. The Emperor's son Saʿd is not forgotten; he is married to Maryam, Shaykha of Qūnka, and his children will rule the frontier

data.heir: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, 22 (16/20/17), no adult traits; wives Magdalena de Borja (daughter of King Alfons of Aragon) and Isabel de Montsoriu (daughter of Francesc de Montsoriu of Catalonia)

emperorsSons.Saʿd ibn Ismāʿīl (16): 83/43/61, married to Maryam, Shaykha of Qūnka

data.emperor: Ismāʿīl ibn Saʿd, 42 (47/100/38), deceitful, goal-oriented, and now just
data.decision: Enough to set thoughts of changing succession aside; his heirs will lead the realm forward if Ismāʿīl can have a long reign (Trent)
data.note: save from before the boys' educations were set (Trent)

source: save of 5 August 1408; Trent's account and screens

title: A new round of expeditions sets out: one south, to follow the coast of Africa further; one to the islands found off the west coast, west of Mali; and two to the islands the Portuguese and Castilian explorers call the Canaries and Madeira

expeditions: the islands west of Mali (Cape Verde)
